caveat: Screening output. Each flagged patch is a suspected land-cover change from satellite classification, and the options are matched from a curated case bank by fixed rules. Save Vietnam's Wildlife reviews every brief before it is used.

overview.run: This run (2025) scored 183 suspected forest-loss patches across 7 sites: 2 in the top priority tier, 31 in the middle and 150 in the lowest. The three sites with the highest-ranked patches are briefed: Tam Diep (42 patches, top priority 64.7); Kim Bang (27 patches, top priority 60.3); and Van Long - Dong Tam (33 patches, top priority 57.0). The other four sites (Cuc Phuong, Hoa Lu / Trang An, Huong Son - Lac Thuy and Pu Luong) hold the remaining 81 patches and are not briefed this run. No option is ready to raise outright yet: each one still has a condition to confirm or is already in place and needs checking. None of the cases has been reviewed by Save Vietnam's Wildlife yet.

sites.tam-diep-forest-nb: **Tam Diep** has 42 suspected quarry patches, 154.9 ha in total; one of them is in the top priority tier. [The restoration deposit for quarries (Decree 08/2022)](https://winrock.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/LuatBVMT-Eng_20230203.pdf) would make the operator pay to restore the cleared site; before raising it, confirm that the quarry holds a licence, so a deposit and a remediation plan exist; and that the deposit is large enough to pay for restoring karst forest. [A conservation-area designation like Kim Bang's](https://en.vietnamplus.vn/ninh-binh-establishes-worlds-largest-delacours-langur-sanctuary-post354875.vnp) would put the forest under a conservation management board; before raising it, confirm that the provincial People's Committee is willing to designate and that conservation organisations sustain the case over several years. [India's fixed no-mining buffer around protected areas](https://www.livelaw.in/pdf_upload/392-in-re-t-n-godavarman-thirumulpad-v-union-of-india-28-apr-2023-471708.pdf) would ban mining within a set distance of the protected area, but it needs groundwork first: the condition "the patch is within a defined buffer of a protected-area boundary" is not met here.
sites.kim-bang: **Kim Bang** has 27 suspected quarry patches, 372.7 ha in total; one of them is in the top priority tier. [Kim Bang's conservation-area designation (November 2026)](https://en.vietnamplus.vn/ninh-binh-establishes-worlds-largest-delacours-langur-sanctuary-post354875.vnp) is already in place here, so the first step is to check whether the flagged patches fall inside the new boundary, which the data behind this run predates. [The restoration deposit for quarries (Decree 08/2022)](https://winrock.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/LuatBVMT-Eng_20230203.pdf) would make the operator pay to restore the cleared site; before raising it, confirm that the quarry holds a licence, so a deposit and a remediation plan exist; and that the deposit is large enough to pay for restoring karst forest. [India's fixed no-mining buffer around protected areas](https://www.livelaw.in/pdf_upload/392-in-re-t-n-godavarman-thirumulpad-v-union-of-india-28-apr-2023-471708.pdf) would ban mining within a set distance of the protected area, but it needs groundwork first: the condition "the patch is within a defined buffer of a protected-area boundary" is not met here.
sites.van-long-dong-tam: **Van Long - Dong Tam** has 33 suspected quarry patches, 55.0 ha in total; the highest-ranked is in the middle priority tier. Of these, 3 lie inside a protected area (Nature Reserve), 10 in a protected-area buffer zone and 20 outside any protected area, and the options differ between them. For the 3 patches inside a protected area (Nature Reserve): [Van Long's community-backed reserve management](https://panorama.solutions/fr/node/5880) is already in place here, so the question is whether it is working: ask the reserve's management board whether it knew of the clearing and what enforcement followed. [The Minerals Law's ban on mining in special-use and protective forest](https://apolatlegal.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/LAW-GEOLOGY-AND-MINERALS.pdf) would make quarrying here a breach of an existing prohibition; before raising it, confirm that the province's land records classify this land as special-use or protective forest. For the 10 patches in a protected-area buffer zone: Van Long's community-backed reserve management covers these patches too. [The restoration deposit for quarries (Decree 08/2022)](https://winrock.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/LuatBVMT-Eng_20230203.pdf) would make the operator pay to restore the cleared site; before raising it, confirm that the quarry holds a licence, so a deposit and a remediation plan exist; and that the deposit is large enough to pay for restoring karst forest. For the 20 patches outside any protected area: The restoration deposit for quarries (Decree 08/2022) applies to these patches too, on the same conditions. [A conservation-area designation like Kim Bang's](https://en.vietnamplus.vn/ninh-binh-establishes-worlds-largest-delacours-langur-sanctuary-post354875.vnp) would put the forest under a conservation management board; before raising it, confirm that the provincial People's Committee is willing to designate and that conservation organisations sustain the case over several years.

options.description: A mineral operation pays a deposit so that environmental remediation of the site is funded. If the operator is dissolved or goes bankrupt, the authority that approved the mine closure plan uses the deposit to do the work [1].
options.howItFits: Whether the quarry holds a licence is not yet known. If it does, a deposit and a remediation plan should already exist, and the request is for the province to check the plan covers the cleared forest and to hold the operator to it. If it does not, this option falls away and the patch is an unlicensed operation.
options.evidence: Article 37 of Decree 08/2022/ND-CP governs paying and refunding the deposit for environmental remediation during mineral mining; under clause 9 the deposit, with its interest, passes to the authority that approved the mine closure plan if the operator is dissolved or bankrupt [1]. In the former Kim Bang area, mineral projects in four localities were to end operations by 31 December 2025 and carry out soil rehabilitation and environmental restoration [2].
options.limitations: The deposit pays for restoration after extraction. It does not stop the clearing, and restored quarry floor is not karst forest. The English translation predates later amendments to the Decree, so the current wording of Article 37 needs checking [1].

options.name: Fixed no-mining distance around protected areas (Supreme Court of India, 2023)
options.description: India's Supreme Court held that mining is not permissible inside national parks and wildlife sanctuaries or within one kilometre of their boundaries [1].
options.howItFits: The patch is quarrying outside a protected-area boundary, which is the gap a fixed no-mining distance closes.
options.evidence: Paragraph 65 of the Court's judgment of 26 April 2023 in the T.N. Godavarman case set the rule, and the order of 28 April 2023 restates it, noting that a ban earlier limited to Goa now applies across India [1]. The Court's order of 26 April 2023 relaxed the uniform one-kilometre eco-sensitive zone for other activities while keeping the mining ban, and noted that India has 104 national parks and 558 wildlife sanctuaries [2].
options.limitations: No measurement of the ruling's effect on forest or wildlife was found. The Court relaxed the uniform zone for other activities [2], so the fixed distance survives only for mining.

options.description: The reserve's management board has the mandate to make decisions in the reserve, and residents, some of them former hunters, take part in protection through community conservation teams [1].

options.limitations: The same source reports that the reserve is affected by smoke, dust and waste from the nearby Gian Khau Industrial Zone [1], so the model has not been shown to hold back industrial pressure such as quarrying.

options.name: Limits on repurposing natural forest (Law on Forestry 2017, Article 14)
options.description: The law bars repurposing natural forest except for projects of national importance, defence and security projects, and urgent projects that meet Government criteria. It lists illegal felling, deforestation and encroachment among prohibited acts [1].
options.howItFits: Loss of natural forest inside a protected area is either an approved repurposing or a prohibited act. The request is for the province to say which, and to produce the approval if there is one.
options.evidence: Law No. 16/2017/QH14 came into force on 1 January 2019 (Article 107) [1]. Article 14(2) restricts repurposing natural forest to the project types above, Article 9(1) prohibits illegally felling, deforesting, exploiting or encroaching forests, and Article 20 gives provincial People's Councils the decision on approving forest repurposing guidelines [1].
options.limitations: The law sets the rules for repurposing; it does not by itself show whether a given clearing was approved. Follow-up depends on ranger capacity, which conservation organisations reported as thin at Kim Bang [2].

options.evidence: Article 37 of Decree 08/2022/ND-CP governs paying and refunding the deposit for environmental remediation during mineral mining; under clause 9 the deposit, with its interest, passes to the authority that approved the mine closure plan if the operator is dissolved or bankrupt [1]. options.name: Fixed no-mining distance around protected areas (Supreme Court of India, 2023)
options.description: India's Supreme Court held that mining is not permissible inside national parks and wildlife sanctuaries or within one kilometre of their boundaries [1].
options.howItFits: The patch is quarrying outside a protected-area boundary, which is the gap a fixed no-mining distance closes.
options.evidence: Paragraph 65 of the Court's judgment of 26 April 2023 in the T.N. Godavarman case set the rule, and the order of 28 April 2023 restates it, noting that a ban earlier limited to Goa now applies across India [1]. The Court's order of 26 April 2023 relaxed the uniform one-kilometre eco-sensitive zone for other activities while keeping the mining ban, and noted that India has 104 national parks and 558 wildlife sanctuaries [2].
options.limitations: No measurement of the ruling's effect on forest or wildlife was found. The Court relaxed the uniform zone for other activities [2], so the fixed distance survives only for mining.

conditions.text: The patch is within a defined buffer of a protected-area boundary
A national body can impose one distance on every province
conditions.note: India's rule came from public-interest litigation in its Supreme Court [1]. No source was found for an equivalent route in Vietnam; the nearest equivalent would be a Government decree or a provincial decision.

briefs.overview: **Van Long - Dong Tam** has 33 suspected quarry patches, 55.0 ha in total; the highest-ranked is in the middle priority tier. Of these, 3 lie inside a protected area (Nature Reserve), 10 in a protected-area buffer zone and 20 outside any protected area, and the options differ between them. For the 3 patches inside a protected area (Nature Reserve): [Van Long's community-backed reserve management](https://panorama.solutions/fr/node/5880) is already in place here, so the question is whether it is working: ask the reserve's management board whether it knew of the clearing and what enforcement followed. [The Minerals Law's ban on mining in special-use and protective forest](https://apolatlegal.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/LAW-GEOLOGY-AND-MINERALS.pdf) would make quarrying here a breach of an existing prohibition; before raising it, confirm that the province's land records classify this land as special-use or protective forest. For the 10 patches in a protected-area buffer zone: Van Long's community-backed reserve management covers these patches too. [The restoration deposit for quarries (Decree 08/2022)](https://winrock.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/LuatBVMT-Eng_20230203.pdf) would make the operator pay to restore the cleared site; before raising it, confirm that the quarry holds a licence, so a deposit and a remediation plan exist; and that the deposit is large enough to pay for restoring karst forest. For the 20 patches outside any protected area: The restoration deposit for quarries (Decree 08/2022) applies to these patches too, on the same conditions. [A conservation-area designation like Kim Bang's](https://en.vietnamplus.vn/ninh-binh-establishes-worlds-largest-delacours-langur-sanctuary-post354875.vnp) would put the forest under a conservation management board; before raising it, confirm that the provincial People's Committee is willing to designate and that conservation organisations sustain the case over several years.
